ActionItem.description:
A PROPOSED follow-up (a recommendation, not an action): no owner, no due date, nothing
executes it. Cites the observations that motivate it.
ActionItem.title: ActionItem

ActionRequest.description:
POST /v1/incidents/{ref}/actions (an SRE, by hand) or .../actions/proposals (the
orchestrator, for the user who started the investigation).

recommendation.description: snapshot shown to the approver; code-written for AI proposals
recommendation.title: Recommendation

ActionRequest.title: ActionRequest

Claim.description:
'This incident and INC-x have the same/different <field>'. Proposed by the model (or by
code when the model is down); KEPT only if code computes the same relation.
Claim.title: Claim

DecisionResult.description:
POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision: the decision, and - when APPROVED - what the
controlled execution did (EXECUTED / FAILED with the reason).
DecisionResult.title: DecisionResult

hidden_edges.description: evidence edges of kinds this caller may not read
hidden_edges.title: Hidden Edges

InvestigationAccepted.description:
202 body: the investigation runs asynchronously. Phase 9: the orchestrator answers
`/investigate` and adds the investigation it started (poll `GET /investigations/{id}`).
InvestigationAccepted.title: InvestigationAccepted

NoChange.description:
Negative evidence ("requests_per_sec stayed within its baseline"): code-written, but it
IS evidence (numbers from metrics), so it is redacted like a sentence (review: it leaked
METRIC data to MANAGER while the METRIC rows were hidden).
NoChange.title: NoChange

PmSentence.description:
One model-written sentence. `refs` = observation refs it cites; `evidence_keys` =
what code mapped them to (used to redact it for a reader without that evidence).
Stored sentences always cite (incident-service refuses empty lists); a REDACTED sentence
in a GET response has both lists emptied, so the ids do not leak either (review).
PmSentence.title: PmSentence

PostmortemDoc.description: GET /v1/incidents/{id}/postmortem. Assembled by code at read time.
PostmortemDoc.title: PostmortemDoc

ReleaseRiskOut.description: GET /api/v1/release-risk/{id}. Readable with code:read (it holds code excerpts).
ReleaseRiskOut.title: ReleaseRiskOut

ReleaseRiskReport.description:
`band` = the advice: risk found, raised to at least MEDIUM when part of the release could
not be checked (unknown is not safe). `findings_band` = risk found in what WAS checked, and
`coverage` says whether everything was - so "we found a problem" and "we could not see" are
never confused (the scan showed the second one dominating on the synthetic history).
ReleaseRiskReport.title: ReleaseRiskReport

ReleaseRiskRequest.description:
Exactly one target:
- pull_request: repository + pull_request (its merge commit)
- range: a release CANDIDATE before it ships - service_key + base_sha (what runs now) +
  head_sha (what would ship); commits after base up to head
- deploy: deploy_key - what that deploy shipped since the previous successful deploy of the
  service, plus its config changes ("would this have been flagged?")
ReleaseRiskRequest.title: ReleaseRiskRequest

RollbackArgs.description: = tool-gateway RollbackIn (the gateway validates the same shape before hashing).
RollbackArgs.title: RollbackArgs

RollbackStep.description:
How to take the risky part back OUT, decided by code from the diff and the deploy:
flag_off (the risky code is behind a flag), redeploy (it is not: only a rollback removes
it), flag_not_read (a flag this deploy changed is not read by the changed code: switching
it back does NOT undo the code change), none (nothing risky to take back).
RollbackStep.title: RollbackStep

RootCause.description: Code-assembled from the stored top hypothesis of the postmortem's investigation.
RootCause.title: RootCause

SearchRequest.description: The caller's groups come from the verified token - never from this body.

rerank.description: null = service default (off until the eval shows a gain)
rerank.title: Rerank

SearchRequest.title: SearchRequest

degraded.description: set when part of the pipeline was skipped
degraded.title: Degraded

untrusted.description: data is untrusted input: wrap it before it reaches a prompt
untrusted.title: Untrusted
